summary: Assert/error inventory of src/interpret.cpp and its decode/execute headers, native and uarch builds. No candidate at Medium or above survived: every abort site of the uarch binary (enumerated from uarch/uarch-ram.elf.objdump) was argued unreachable, on reachable states and, except for a PMA table that machine creation cannot produce, on unreachable ones too. One Low, cross-cutting build finding is reported because it contradicts the working premise that native asserts are compiled out.

candidates.title: Packaged emulator disables asserts only in interpret.cpp: asserts are live aborts in every other honest-operator translation unit, and inline functions of the shared state-access headers get two different bodies
candidates.component: Emulator build (src/Makefile, Dockerfile) and the state-access headers shared by interpret.cpp with machine.cpp, hash-tree.cpp, uarch-step.cpp, send-cmio-response.cpp
candidates.location: src/Makefile:208-222 (default build type is relwithdebinfo; 'INTERPRET_CXXFLAGS+=-DNDEBUG # disable asserts only for interpret.cpp'; only release=yes adds -DNDEBUG to DEFS); Makefile:135-139 ('so the emulator is packaged correctly by default'); Dockerfile:64 and :69 (make ... debug=$DEBUG coverage=$COVERAGE sanitize=$SANITIZE, then debian-package: no release=yes). Inline functions with assert() in headers that interpret.cpp includes: state-access.hpp:92 and collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp:95 (do_write_x: assert(i != 0)), collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp:453 (do_read_pma: assert(index < PMA_MAX)), replay-step-state-access.hpp:581, access-log.hpp:59,64, page-hash-tree-cache.hpp:238,244. Live asserts in other honest-operator TUs include machine.cpp:2575-3009 (collect_mcycle_root_hashes / collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes), hash-tree.cpp:112,123,197,207,609-664,912-952, back-merkle-tree.cpp:136-142, uarch-state-access.hpp:54, record-send-cmio-state-access.hpp:163-174, dirty-page-tree.hpp:353.
candidates.description: The Docker image and Debian package are built with the default build type, relwithdebinfo. In that build NDEBUG is defined for interpret.cpp alone, so (1) every assert() in the other translation units of the honest operator (machine.cpp with both hash collectors, hash-tree.cpp, back-merkle-tree.cpp, the uarch state accesses, send-cmio-response) is an active abort() of the node process, not a compiled-out check; and (2) inline member functions that contain assert() and live in headers included both by interpret.cpp (NDEBUG) and by other TUs (no NDEBUG) are compiled with two different bodies, an ODR violation: for any out-of-line copy the linker keeps whichever object comes first, so whether such an assert is active inside the interpreter depends on inlining decisions and link order. The campaign has treated native asserts as compiled out ('natively (asserts off)'); that holds only for interpret.cpp itself, or for release=yes builds, which no shipped artifact uses.
candidates.trigger: None found inside the INVINTERP files. A trigger would be any guest program, input, log or stored state that falsifies one of the live asserts on the honest operator's path. The ones tied to interpreter execution were checked and are not reachable: the interpreter never calls write_x(0) (all 41 write_x call sites carry an rd guard or are selected by the jump table, and all 65536 jump-table entries were checked against an independent RVC/RV64 decoder: no _rdN label with rd=0, no compressed handler that writes rd reached with rd=0); find_pma never passes an index >= PMA_MAX to the collector's read_pma (a reproducible machine has at most 24 PMAs: RAM, DTB, 8 flash drives, 8 NVRAMs, 2 cmio buffers, HTIF, CLINT, PLIC, PMAs); the interpreter never writes TLB_UNVERIFIED_PAGE to a TLB slot.
candidates.reachability: The build configuration itself is always present in the shipped artifacts. No reachable state was found that fails an assert, so no crash is demonstrated. The asserts in machine.cpp, hash-tree.cpp and the log state accesses belong to other angles and were only listed, not analysed.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded: it needs no API misuse, no foreign snapshot and no host fault; it is a property of the build the emulator documents as the packaged one.
rating_steps.2_role: Honest operator: AUDIT.md lists 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program, hash tree, log producers, collect_mcycle_root_hashes and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes' in that role.
rating_steps.3_high_medium: No listed case fits as it stands. If one of these asserts fails only on demonstrably unreachable states it would be 'A crash, hang, or memory-safety defect in the emulator that only demonstrably unreachable states trigger' (High). For the C++ verifiers (Support), R10 says 'Its outcome, including whether it rejects, must not depend on its build configuration, such as the build type or whether assertions are enabled'; an assert that data in a log can fail would break that sentence, rated Medium at most for a support verifier.
rating_steps.4_critical: Not shown. It becomes Critical if any live assert is reachable from guest behaviour or from data the operator must process: R8 'No guest action may corrupt host memory, crash or hang the host', and section 8 'A crash, hang, out-of-bounds read, or unbounded allocation caused by data from other parties that the honest operator must process'.
rating_steps.5_low: Low as reported: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model', because no failing assert was found.

candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Critical or High only if another angle finds one of these live asserts reachable; this entry is mainly a correction of the 'native asserts are off' premise)
candidates.threat_to_goal: No direct threat shown. It removes a margin: an internal-consistency assert that a guest, an input or relayed data can falsify stops the honest operator (completeness failure, section 1) in the packaged build, while the same condition is silently ignored in a release=yes build, so the two builds of the same version would also behave differently.
candidates.evidence: In the harness's in-tree build (default flags): nm src/interpret.o shows no __assert_fail reference, while machine.o, hash-tree.o, uarch-step.o and send-cmio-response.o each reference it; interpret.o and machine.o share weak inline symbols of the state-access templates (for example device_state_access<state_access>::do_set_mip). src/Makefile lines 208-222 and Dockerfile line 64 read as quoted in location.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: build as the Dockerfile does (default flags) and fail (exit 1) if objects other than interpret.o reference __assert_fail while interpret.o does not, i.e. require one NDEBUG setting for all translation units of libcartesi; equivalently check that 'nm -D --undefined-only libcartesi.so | grep __assert_fail' is empty in the packaged build. A behavioural test needs a concrete failing assert from another angle.

verified_without_finding: uarch abort sites: uarch/uarch-ram.elf.objdump has 3 ebreak instructions (abort itself twice, and the __builtin_trap after ua_halt_ECALL) and 13 calls to abort in 9 functions: assert_no_brk (5), get_highest_priority_irq_num's assert(false) inlined in interpret_loop (1), the final mcycle assert of interpret (1), soft-float normalize/normalize2 (2 stubs shared by f32 and f64, called from add, mul, div, sqrt, fma and cvt_i_f), the make_mock_address_range lambda in do_read_pma (1), device_state_access do_read_memory/do_write_memory (2, VirtIO only), __cxa_pure_virtual (1). Each was argued unreachable: interrupt invariants hold for every transition (all mip/mie/mideleg/mstatus.xIE/privilege changes return success_and_serve_interrupts or cannot enable an interrupt; HTIF/CLINT/PLIC statuses are propagated by every store form: S, C.S, FS, C.FS, AMO, SC); WARL masks keep mip & mie inside the six interrupt bits; normalize's shift >= 0 was derived for every caller; the PMA table is validated at creation (init_pmas_contents) and read-only to the guest.
Instruction set of the uarch binary: only the 49 supported rv64i mnemonics, no .word/.insn.

Jump table (src/interpret-jump-table.hpp): all 49152 compressed entries equal an independent RV64C+Zcb decoder (only the C_NOP/C_HINT names are swapped, both no-ops); rd0/rdN labels of 32-bit opcodes always match the rd field; reserved encodings (C.ADDI4SPN nzuimm=0, C.ADDIW rd=0, C.LUI/C.ADDI16SP imm=0, C.LWSP/C.LDSP rd=0, C.JR rs1=0) are ILLEGAL.

Immediate and register field decoders (interpret.cpp 612-884) compared with spec-derived references for all 65536 compressed patterns with zero, all-ones and random upper 16 bits, and 2e7 random 32-bit instructions: 0 mismatches (compressed handlers do not depend on the 2 extra fetched bytes).

soft-float.hpp differential test against the host FPU (x86-64 SSE/FMA, fenv rounding modes and flags): add, sub, mul, div, sqrt, fma, eq/lt/le, f32<->f64, int->float in RNE/RTZ/RDN/RUP, float->int in all five modes against RISC-V saturation rules; 9.12 million checks, 0 mismatches, once with native __int128 and once with -DAVOID_NATIVE_UINT128_T=1 (the Fortran Int128 emulation and the quotient-based remainder the uarch build uses). The discarded return value of mant_normalize_subnormal in sfloat_cvt_f64_f32 is benign.

Fetch cache versus TLB_CODE: every TLB_CODE change (set_prv, satp MODE change, sfence.vma, a fetch that replaces the slot) invalidates or rewrites the native fetch cache, so the per-instruction uarch run and the native loop fetch through the same translation; shadow_tlb_verify_slot accepts exactly what replace_tlb_entry writes for each set.

Recent fixes re-read for regressions: MTIP level semantics (0dfebe1), failed SC through write_mode::skip_write (2175acb), page-table entries outside RAM (de2a679), sip write mask (75e9f89), icycleinstret on interrupts (a857edf). No inconsistency between native and uarch paths found.

CSR write/read masks (riscv-constants.hpp, riscv-warl.hpp): sstatus cannot change MPP/MPRV/TVM/TW/TSR; mideleg limited to S bits; medeleg excludes M ecall; ASIDLEN=0 so satp flushes on MODE change only, which the privileged spec permits.

Worst-case uarch cycles per mcycle: no guest-extensible loop in the interpreter (find_pma <= 33 iterations, page walk <= 4 levels, flushes 768 slots, sqrt 64 and Int128 division <= 128 iterations); consistent with earlier measurements far below 2^20.
not_covered: The other state-access layers the interpreter is instantiated with (record_step, replay_step, collect_mcycle_hashes, uarch state accesses) beyond the functions the uarch bridge and native state_access share; machine.cpp TLB helpers were read only for mark_write_tlb_dirty_page and init_pmas_contents.

The live asserts outside interpret.cpp listed in candidate 1 (machine.cpp collectors, hash-tree.cpp page-cache borrow asserts 'page hash-tree cache has no entries to lend', back-merkle-tree.cpp, record/replay state accesses): not analysed for reachability; they belong to the machine, hash-tree and access angles. In a release=yes build the hash-tree asserts on an empty optional become undefined behaviour instead of an abort; not analysed.

No dynamic native-versus-uarch differential run was made in this round (earlier rounds ran fuzzers); in particular PLIC claim/complete with config-set girqpend/girqsrvd and CLINT msip/mtimecmp through AMO, SC and float stores were checked by reading only.
soft-float RMM rounding for add/mul/div/sqrt/fma was checked by reading (the host FPU has no RMM); fmin/fmax, fclass and fsgnj were checked by reading only.
Whether a failed SC may set the PTE D bit and fill the write TLB (it does, on a TLB miss) under the privileged specification's 'exact' A/D update wording: not resolved offline, not reported.
The uarch interpreter itself (uarch-step.cpp, uarch-interpret.cpp) and its ECALL handlers, the ZKARCHITECTURE build, the CODE_COVERAGE uarch build, and DUMP_* instrumented builds.

Linker-script orphan sections of the uarch image (uarch-ram.ld lists only .text/.rodata/.sdata/.bss/.tdata, while template code sits in .text._Z* sections and .data/.sbss are orphans): layout depends on the linker's orphan placement; relevant to reproducible builds (R13), not examined further.
Host builds other than x86-64 GCC (clang, aarch64, big-endian is rejected by static_assert), and -march=native builds (native=yes).
